criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: it does not improve after treating it at home for a few weeks

criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: it's stopping you doing your day-to-day activities

criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: you're worried about the pain or you're struggling to cope

criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: you've lost weight without trying to

criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: there's a lump or swelling in your back, or your back has changed shape

criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: it does not improve after resting or is worse at night

criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: it's worse when sneezing, coughing or pooing

criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: it's coming from the top of your back (between your shoulders), rather than your lower back

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from 111 if:
criteria.text: you feel hot, cold, shivery or generally unwell

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from 111 if:
criteria.text: it's severe pain that starts suddenly, or it's getting worse quickly

criteria.nhs_section: Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
criteria.text: pain, tingling, weakness or numbness in both legs

criteria.nhs_section: Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
criteria.text: a loss of feeling around your genitals or anus

criteria.nhs_section: Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
criteria.text: changes in your bladder or bowels, such as difficulty peeing, or peeing or pooing yourself

criteria.nhs_section: Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
criteria.text: changes in how your penis or vagina feels during sex, not being able to get or keep an erection, or not being able to orgasm

criteria.nhs_section: Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
criteria.text: chest pain

criteria.nhs_section: Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
criteria.text: it started after a serious accident, such as a car accident

criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: knee pain does not improve within a few weeks

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Get advice from 111 now if:
criteria.text: your knee is very painful

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Get advice from 111 now if:
criteria.text: you cannot move your knee or put any weight on it

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Get advice from 111 now if:
criteria.text: your knee is badly swollen or has changed shape

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Get advice from 111 now if:
criteria.text: your knee locks, gives way or painfully clicks – painless clicking is normal

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Get advice from 111 now if:
criteria.text: you have a very high temperature (or feel hot, cold or shivery) and have redness or heat around your knee – this can be a sign of infection

criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: neck pain or stiffness does not go away after a few weeks

criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: painkillers like paracetamol or ibuprofen have not worked

criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: you're worried about the pain

criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: you have other symptoms, like pins and needles or a cold arm – this could be something more serious

criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: shoulder pain is getting worse or does not improve after 2 weeks

criteria.nhs_section: Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
criteria.text: it's very difficult to move your arm or shoulder

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
criteria.text: you have sudden or very bad shoulder pain

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
criteria.text: you cannot move your arm

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
criteria.text: your arm or shoulder has changed shape or is badly swollen

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
criteria.text: you have pins and needles that do not go away

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
criteria.text: there's no feeling in your arm or shoulder

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
criteria.text: your arm or shoulder is hot or cold to touch

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
criteria.text: the pain started after an injury or accident, like a fall

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
criteria.text: you develop severe pain in both shoulders

criteria.nhs_section: Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
criteria.text: you feel feverish or unwell
